npmerger — package plan

Source: PLAN.md

Proposed R package for finding, classifying, and analyzing nonprofit mergers using IRS 990 e-file data (Schedule N + core 990), built on panel990 (retrieval/panels) and fiscal (fiscal-health metrics).

Background reviewed: Schedule N 2025 form + instructions, the 2018 outcomes draft (CEM + DiD design), the 2020 IU slides, the financial-ratio sources memo, Wilder/MAP Minnesota study (merger = “integration of two or more organizations into one legal entity in which at least one ceases to exist”, plus transfer of programs and of assets or staff), and 01-build-merger-panel.rmd (2020 prototype on the old AWS index).

1. What the experiments found (NCCS efile v3_1, tax years 2019–2021)

Scripts are in dev/experiments/ (they expect env var S = a scratch data directory).

Data layout (panel990 tables)

Table Grain Contents
SN-P01-T00-…DISSOLUTION 1 per filing Part I lines 2a–2d (successor director/employee/owner/comp), 3–6
SN-P01-T01-…DISSOLUTION 1 per asset line Part I line 1: desc, date, FMV, method, recipient EIN/name/address/IRC section
SN-P02-T00/T01-DISPOSITION-OF-ASSETS same, for Part II
SN-P03-T99-SUPPLEMENTAL-INFO narrative Part III text (names of people moving, line 3 explanations)
SN-P99-T00 — empty, ignore
F9-P00 header 1 per filing F9_00_RETURN_FINAL_X, F9_00_YEAR_FORMATION, address
F9-P01 summary 1 per filing revenue, expenses, assets BOY/EOY, liabilities, employees
F9-P07-T01-COMPENSATION 1 per person name, title, position flags, comp

Volumes: about 3–3.8k Part I filings and 1.2–1.4k Part II filings per year, so 14,399 Schedule N filings in 2019–21. 1,004 filings fill in both parts, even though the instructions say not to. 94 EINs file Schedule N in more than one year.

Data-quality issues the package has to handle - Checkbox encodings are mixed: 0/1, true/false, and NA. - The T00 and T01 tables don’t line up. 1,406 Part I filings have no asset rows, and 650 have asset rows but no T00 row. Build the filing universe as the union of OBJECTIDs. - 28% of recipient rows have no usable EIN. The IRC section is free text, with around 40 spellings of 501(c)(3), plus “LLC”, “INDIVIDUAL”, “GOVERNMENT” and others. - FMV has negatives and implausible outliers (max $11B). Check it against the donor’s beginning-of-year assets (the “coverage” ratio). - 225 transfers go to the donor’s own EIN (reorganizations). - 52% of Part I filers are 990-EZ filers, so you need the EZ summary and EZ Part VII tables too, not just the F9 tables. - Recipients: 81% of the top nonprofit recipients are in efile. 98% of those keep filing after the transfer, and 6% were formed within a year of it.

Prototype classifier (rule-based), with validation signals that are not used by the rules:

Label N % Final return Donor files later Median coverage (FMV/BOY assets) Part VII person overlap*
closure 5,784 40.2 .95 .04 0.22 9%
asset_transfer 3,701 25.7 .96 .03 0.84 40%
asset_disposition (Part II only) 3,250 22.6 .21 .69 0.76 —
merger2 1,373 9.5 .96 .02 0.95 87%
mergerN 256 1.8 .95 .04 0.91 92%
mergerN into new entity 35 0.2 .94 .03 0.99 100%

* Share of donor→recipient pairs where at least one donor Part VII person (t-1..t) appears on the recipient’s Part VII (t..t+1), matched on first + last name.

Takeaways: 1. Schedule N lines 2a–2c are a good merger signal, but under-reported. About 40% of “asset transfers” to a continuing nonprofit with no box checked still show shared leadership on Part VII. Part VII overlap should be a second evidence channel, which could add roughly 1,000 mergers over three years. 2. “Recipient continues operating” is nearly always true for nonprofit recipients, so it adds little for telling cases apart. The useful signals are leadership continuity, how concentrated the transfer is (top-recipient FMV share), and coverage. 3. mergerN (2+ dissolving donors to one recipient in the same year) is real: 371 recipient-years. Many are system consolidations (hospital systems, chapters folding into a national office). 132 recipients appear as acquirers in more than one year. That is worth a serial_acquirer / affiliate flag. 4. Donor size is small for transfers and closures (median revenue $4k–$10k) and larger for mergers (about $87k for merger2 and $370k for mergerN). Recipients are typically 50–100× larger, which matches the 2020 slides.

2. Definitions (proposed)

Unit of analysis: a transaction pair (donor EIN → recipient EIN, Schedule N tax year), grouped into a merger event.

  • MERGER_ID = YEAR-FROMEIN-TOEIN (9-digit EINs, YEAR = donor’s Schedule N tax year), one per pair.
  • MERGER_GROUP_ID = YEAR-TOEIN links all donors folding into one recipient (mergerN and consolidations).
  • Merger year (t = 0) = the donor’s Schedule N tax year. The asset distribution date gets mapped onto the recipient’s fiscal calendar, so the recipient’s t = 0 is the fiscal year that contains the distribution date. Both are stored.

Transaction types returned by classify_transactions(), one label per filing, plus evidence columns:

Label Rule sketch
merger2 Part I (dissolved), a dominant nonprofit recipient (≥50% of FMV), leadership continuity (2a/2b/2c or Part VII overlap), and the recipient has only this donor that year
mergerN same as merger2, but the recipient has ≥2 dissolving donors in the window (t ± 1)
consolidation mergerN where the recipient is newly formed (formation year or first filing ≥ t−1). This covers your “two orgs close and form a third” case
asset_transfer Part I, a dominant nonprofit recipient, no leadership-continuity evidence
closure Part I, with no assets, assets only to individuals/businesses/government/unknown, or assets spread across many charities (top share < 50%)
asset_disposition Part II only (the org continues). Subtypes: sale (business or individual recipient), transfer_np (nonprofit recipient), spinoff (nonprofit recipient + leadership continuity)
reorganization recipient EIN = donor EIN, or a disregarded entity
other / inconsistent for example Part I filed but the donor keeps filing for 2+ years, or there are no usable rows

Every threshold is an argument (merger_rules()), and the output keeps the evidence columns (LEADER_SN, LEADER_P7, TOP_SHARE, COVERAGE, N_DONORS, R_NEW, FINAL_RETURN, DONOR_FILES_LATER). Users can then re-label without re-running the pipeline, and run sensitivity analyses on strict vs. broad definitions.

3. Package architecture

npmerger/
  DESCRIPTION   Imports: data.table, panel990, fiscal; Suggests: duckdb, arrow, testthat, knitr
  R/
    retrieve.R      get_schedule_n(years, ...)       -> sn_raw (6 SN tables via panel990::download_tables/read_tables)
                    get_core(eins, years, tables)    -> header, P01/EZ summary, P07 for selected EINs only (parquet pushdown)
    clean.R         sn_flag(), clean_ein(), parse_irc_section(), sn_transactions(sn_raw)
                    -> long table: 1 row per asset line, Part I + II stacked, with recipient type
    recipients.R    recover_recipient_ein(): name+ZIP/state fuzzy match vs efile header (and BMF) for the 28% missing
    features.R      sn_filings(): filing-level features (parts, flags, N recipients, top share, FMV totals, coverage)
                    leader_overlap(): Part VII person matching donor -> recipient (name normalization, window)
    classify.R      merger_rules(), classify_transactions(features, rules) -> label + evidence
    cases.R         build_merger_cases(): pairs, MERGER_ID, MERGER_GROUP_ID, merger years, role table
    assets.R        transfer_value(): FMV to the recipient, by asset class (cash / receivables / investments /
                    real estate / other) with outlier flags; book-value fallback (donor BOY assets − liabilities)
    tables.R        sched_n_table()          YEAR, OBJECTID, EIN2, TYPE (+ subtype, evidence)
                    donor_attributes()        merger ID, SN year, rev/exp/assets t-5..t (wide), address, age, NTEE
                    recipient_attributes()    same, recipient EIN
                    merger_part7()            people x year, t-2..t+2, ROLE, TIME_FROM_MERGER, IN_BOTH flag
                    merger_fiscal_panel()     donor (t-5..0) + recipient (t-5..t+5) stacked; fiscal::compute_all_panel()
                                              plus staff exp, exec pay (P07 / Part IX), grants, overhead, debt
    pipeline.R      build_merger_data(years) -> list of all tables + manifest (row counts, drops, per step)
  inst/extdata/     small fixture (about 200 filings, all labels) for tests and examples
  tests/testthat/   flag parsing, IRC parsing, classifier truth table, ID format, panel windows
  vignettes/        01-identifying-mergers, 02-building-panels, 03-did-example (matched comparison)
  data-raw/         script to build the fixture + an IRC-section lookup table

Design choices: - data.table throughout, matching panel990 and fiscal. Return plain data.frames/data.tables with documented columns. - Fetch selectively. Schedule N is tiny (about 1 MB/yr), but header, summary and P07 are 50–100 MB/yr. Download Schedule N for all years, derive the EIN set, then read core tables with an EIN filter (duckdb parquet pushdown, cache = "none" option). - Keep the stages separate. raw → transactions → features → labels → cases → output tables. Each stage is a function, so users can step in anywhere (for example, swap in their own classifier). - Get metrics from fiscal, not reimplement them. fiscal now defaults to the current efile release (v3_1), the same as panel990. See section 7 for calibration and smoothing. - NTEE, ruling year and address come from the BMF through panel990::bmf_merge() / fiscal::get_clean_ntee(). Org age = tax year − min(formation year, ruling year).

4. Build sequence

  1. ✅ Skeleton + retrieval/cleaning (get_schedule_n, sn_transactions, flag/IRC/EIN parsers) with tests.
  2. ✅ Filing features + classifier (rules from section 2) and sched_n_table(). Hand-validated on 300 filings, with three rule changes as a result; see section 9.
  3. ✅ Merger evidence wired into the classifier (get_evidence_tables(), merger_features()):
    • Part VII overlap: leader_overlap(). The F9 Part VII table also covers EZ filers: 89% of merger donors and recipients have rows.
    • Multi-party counts: add_donor_counts().
    • New-entity detection and filing history: add_filing_history().
    • Corroboration: add_corroboration().
    • Affiliation: add_affiliation().
    • Mission similarity: add_mission_similarity().
    Real-data check on 2021 (5,167 filings; script dev/run-2021.R): closure 2,160; asset_disposition 1,090; asset_transfer 938; merger2 858; mergerN 107; consolidation 14. Of these, 54 mergers rest on corroboration rather than leadership. Affiliated pairs make up 37% of merger2, 76% of mergerN, and 4% of closures. 98% of merger donors file a final return. Evidence retrieval takes about 2.5 minutes cold (from the parquet cache) and 0.4 minutes warm.
  4. ✅ Cases, IDs, and asset values:
    • get_core(), org_years(), merger_measures().
    • build_merger_cases(), which places the merger year on the recipient’s fiscal calendar.
    • transfer_value() and asset_class(). Classifying transferred value moved the “other” bucket from 31% to 3%.
  5. ✅ Attribute tables: merger_attributes() and get_bmf(). NTEE coverage is 97–98%.
  6. ✅ Part VII panel (merger_part7()) and fiscal panel (merger_fiscal_panel(), smooth_trailing()).
  7. ✅ Recipient EIN recovery (recover_recipient_ein()), by unique name + ZIP, then name + state. It recovers only about 1,200 lines (1.2%): of the lines with no EIN, about 40% have no recipient name, and many name churches, governments, or “various”. Most missing-EIN recipients do not file 990s, so the 23% that remain missing is largely a data limit.
  8. ✅ Wrapper and documentation:
    • build_merger_data(), plus offline example data (npmerger_example(), built by data-raw/example.R).
    • Vignette and site.
    • Full-years run (dev/run-all-years.R) and descriptives (dev/descriptives.R); see section 8.

5. Other 990 fields (tested 2026-11-20, dev/experiments/06-other-fields.R)

Decision: leadership continuity = Schedule N lines 2a–2c or Part VII overlap (merger_rules(leader = "either")). With that rule, 2019–21 counts are: closure 5,784; asset_disposition 3,250; asset_transfer 2,632; merger2 2,306; mergerN 427.

The table below shows each field’s rate by label. “Recip.” is measured at the recipient in the merger year.

Field merger2 mergerN asset_transfer closure Verdict
Schedule R Part II: donor and recipient list each other as related orgs .35 .64 .08 .03 Use. Separates intra-system consolidation from arm’s-length merger
Schedule O text mentions merg/consolidat/acquir/affiliat (donor) .33 .54 .10 .04 Use as tiebreaker evidence (all-filer baseline .06)
Same, recipient’s Schedule O .28 .53 .13 .01 Use
Part VI line 4: significant changes to governing documents (recip., t vs t-2) .12 vs .04 .13 vs .05 .02 vs .09 .04 Use, about 3× lift at t
Schedule A: donor is a 509(a)(3) supporting org .18 .25 .09 .05 Use as affiliation flag
Part XII: recipient’s audit is consolidated .34 .63 .30 .25 Descriptive (systems)
Mission-text similarity (Jaccard, donor vs recipient; random = 0) .07 .09 .03 .00 Use as relatedness measure (horizontal vs. other)
Part III: significant new programs (recip., t vs t-2) .06 vs .02 .05 vs .11 .02 .01 Weak, noisy
Part VI line 1a: board grew t-2 → t+1 .40 .41 .38 .52 Not useful
Part XI line 9: other changes in net assets ≈ FMV received (±50%) .23 .08 .08 .02 Use only to validate transfer_value()
Part IV lines 31/32 or final return without Schedule N — — — — No gap: 99–100% have Schedule N

What this means for the package: - Add an affiliation dimension, separate from the label: AFFILIATED = Schedule R link | supporting org | same group exemption number | chapters (Part VI 10a). About a third of merger2 cases and two-thirds of mergerN cases are within one family of organizations. Analyses will usually want to split or drop them. This answers the earlier open question: keep the labels, and add a flag. - Add corroborating evidence columns: SO_MERGER_TEXT_DONOR, SO_MERGER_TEXT_RECIP, and GOV_DOC_CHANGE_RECIP (Part VI line 4 at the recipient, t or t+1). Decision: allow promotion. An asset_transfer becomes a merger label when ≥2 of the 3 signals agree (merger_rules(promote = TRUE, min_corroborate = 2)). The output records BASIS = "corroborated" (vs "leader") and N_CORROBORATE. MISSION_SIM is descriptive only and does not count toward promotion. - Tested on 2021: 54 of 999 asset transfers (5%) are promoted. They look like mergers on measures the rule doesn’t use: 69% of donors end the year with near-zero assets, vs 37% for unpromoted transfers (65% for merger2), and median donor revenue is $61k vs $5k ($47k for merger2). One signal alone would promote 163 cases, which have weaker profiles (47% assets gone, $12k revenue), so the threshold stays at 2. - The universe is complete from Schedule N. Use Part IV and the final-return flag only for validation.

Not tested, but worth adding to the panels: - Part V line 2a W-3 employee count (F9_05_NUM_EMPL) and Part I line 5 employees. These measure staff absorbed by the recipient. - Part VIII line 1g non-cash contributions and Schedule M at the recipient. These are where in-kind asset transfers show up. - Header F9_00_GROUP_EXEMPT_NUM / group returns (chapters), and the name-change / DBA fields (recipients that rename after a merger). - Schedule R Part V (transfers with related orgs), to cross-check transfer amounts within affiliated families. - Schedule D Part V (endowments): restricted funds that move with the merger. - Schedule H (hospitals), for a hospital-specific subsample. - Schedule B contributor names are redacted in public data, so it isn’t usable.

7. Fiscal health index and smoothing (tested 2026-11-20, dev/experiments/07-fiscal-index-smoothing.R)

Is the index calibrated? No. fiscal 0.0.2 has a full measurement workflow: fiscal_diagnostics() → fiscal_triage() → fiscal_dimensions() → fiscal_health_fit() → fiscal_weights() → fiscal_health_score() → fiscal_health_index(). But no fitted model ships with it. The only bundled data are dat10k (10,000 orgs, tax year 2023) and part010810. The docs say triage and dimension discovery “require review and substantive judgment”, so nothing is automated. - I fit the workflow on dat10k with all defaults. It runs end to end: 48 winsorized ratios, 3 PCA dimensions, and 29 standalone indicators. With default equal weights, the standalones dominate the composite. So the defaults are a starting point, not a calibration. - To do: calibrate once on a stated reference sample, review triage, dimensions and weights, and save the fit. Then score every org-year with it. Options for the reference sample: a full single-year cross-section of all 990 filers; a pooled pre-period such as 2018–19; or dat10k.

Can we get metrics for every year and track change? Yes, but use the right layer: - compute_all_panel() gives the raw ratios for every org-year. Its _w / _z / _p columns are re-estimated within each year: percentile and z-score are relative to that year’s cross-section. They are good for ranking but not for tracking absolute change over time. - fiscal_health_score() with a fixed fit applies the stored centers, scales and coefficients without re-estimating. This is the comparable-over-time index. I tested it on 769 merger orgs (3,142 org-years, 2018–23) scored against the 2023 calibration, and it produced an index for every year.

Smoothing. panel990::panel_smooth() is centered only (odd window, positions t-1, t, t+1). It also counts rows rather than calendar years, so filing gaps get bridged. There is no trailing option, in the installed version or on GitHub main. For merger panels this leaks post-merger information into pre-merger years. I compared on recipients (k = 3), measuring partial correlation of the t-1 index with the year-t index, controlling for t-2:

raw trailing (t-2..t) centered (t-1..t+1)
Correlation of t-1 with year t (leakage) .53 .47 .61
Mean index at t-2 (recipients) .21 .20 .38 (inflated)
Within-org year-to-year SD of index .88 .33 .33
  • A trailing window cuts noise as much as centered does (−63% volatility), with no look-ahead.
  • Trailing does lag real changes: the post-merger rise is spread over k years (trailing .26 → .29 → .31 for t = 0..2).
  • Plan:
    1. Add align = c("left", "center", "right") to panel990::panel_smooth() (default "center"). "right" is the trailing window, counted by calendar year. This was requested in panel990. npmerger’s smooth_trailing() calls it when the installed panel990 supports "right", and otherwise uses an equivalent internal version.
    2. In merger_fiscal_panel(), offer smooth = "trailing" (default k = 3).
    3. Use trailing-smoothed values for matching covariates and baselines (t-2), and raw values for event-time outcome estimates. Otherwise the lag smears the merger effect.

8. Full-years run (Schedule N 2010–2024, e-file v3_1; v2 rules, 2026-11-21)

dev/run-all-years.R took 55 minutes on a warm cache (8.3 GB, 2009–2025). Rules: the v2 defaults from section 9 (min_top_share = 0.75, final_as_termination, sn_text, promote = FALSE).

Scale: - 60,235 Schedule N filings; 12,346 merger filings: merger2 9,690; mergerN 2,382; consolidation 274. (v1 rules: 12,059.) - Other labels: closure 26,021; asset_disposition 12,320; asset_transfer 9,548. - These become 12,228 donor→recipient cases in 10,651 merger events. - Mergers grew from about 360 a year (2010) to about 1,050 (2024). - 39% of merger2 and 63% of mergerN are between affiliated organizations.

Descriptives (dev/descriptives.R; sizes are for year t-1, the last full year before the merger):

Closing org (donor) Recipient
Revenue: median (p25–p75) $264k ($59k–$1.29m) $5.3m ($0.82m–$26.3m)
Assets: median $443k $8.2m
Revenue: mean / 5%-trimmed mean $26.5m / $1.24m $105m / $24.8m
  • Size gap. The median recipient has 10.4× the donor’s revenue (p25 2.5×, p75 65×). The recipient is larger in 89% of mergers, more than 10× larger in 51%, and more than 100× larger in 21%. The ratio is smaller for consolidations (1.6–2.0×) and larger for affiliated mergers (17.5× two-party, 21× multi-party).
  • Multi-organization mergers.
    • 8.1% of merger events have two or more closing donors, and those events account for 19.6% of all closing organizations.
    • Group size: 2 donors in 5.9% of events, 3 in 1.3%, 4 or more in 0.9%.
    • 115 consolidations into a new entity, involving 273 donors.
  • Part VII joiners (11,132 mergers with both rosters observed).
    • On average 2.2 donor people newly appear on the recipient’s Part VII after the merger (median 1). 57% of mergers have at least one joiner.
    • About 16% of the donor’s roster joins (median donor roster: 11 people).
    • Separately, 58% of mergers already had at least one person on both rosters before the merger (mean 2.9). Affiliated mergers average about 5 such people.
  • CEO / executive director.
    • A donor CEO or ED can be identified in 4,833 mergers: 82% by title, the rest as the highest-paid officer.
    • 55% of those CEOs appear at the recipient after the merger. Of those, 72% are listed as CEO or ED there, 11% as another officer or staff, and 7% as a board member.
    • The rate is 76% for affiliated two-party mergers, 37% for unaffiliated ones, and 60–64% for consolidations.
  • Asset transfers.
    • Median $319k; 5%-trimmed mean $1.9m; mean $10.9m.
    • $119bn in total across 10,851 positive, unflagged transfers. 678 transfers are flagged as outliers.
    • The median transfer is 93% of the donor’s t-1 assets.
    • As a share of the recipient’s t-1 assets: median 6.4%. 26% of transfers are under 1%, 26% are 10–50%, and 18% are 50% or more. Consolidations are the high end (median 35–39%), since the recipient is new.

9. Classifier validation (step 2; 2026-11-20, dev/validation/)

Design. - 300 Schedule N filings from 2010–2024: 50 drawn at random from each v1 label (merger2, mergerN, consolidation, asset_transfer, closure, asset_disposition). - Drawn only from filings with some narrative: Schedule N Part III text, or Schedule O sentences about dissolution, merger, or transfer. The share with narrative is 36% of closures, 46% of asset transfers, 65% of dispositions, and 84–95% of the merger types. - Each case is a text packet: form header, asset lines, Part III, and Schedule O excerpts. The classifier label is not shown. Packets are labeled blind against codebook.md (merger, asset transfer, closure, asset disposition, reorganization, unclear), with flags for multi-party, new entity, people moving, and programs continuing. - Labeling was done by model readers, not people. A human spot-check of hand-labels.csv is still worthwhile, especially the low-confidence rows (55 of 300). - “Weighted” figures reweight each stratum to its population size.

v1 results. - Agreement: 62% (60% weighted). - Precision: merger 66% (56% weighted), asset transfer 52%, closure 66%, disposition 58%. - Main errors: 1. Part-II-only filers that ended. All 12 with the final-return box checked were terminations (7 mergers, 4 transfers, 1 closure), not dispositions. 2. Asset transfer → closure. 10 of the 11 dissolutions with a top-recipient share between 0.5 and 0.75 read as dispersed closures, and none as mergers. The v1 rule also skipped the share test whenever there was only one nonprofit recipient, even if most value went to vendors or individuals. 3. Merger language on Schedule N itself. Some filings say “transfer due to merger”, “plan merger”, “lodge merged” and so on in the asset description or Part III, but have no leadership evidence. Every such terminated filing with one successor (51 of 51) was read as a merger. This is partly circular, since the readers saw that text, but it is the filer’s own statement. 4. Promotion by corroboration. Only 1 of 8 promoted cases read as a merger. 5. Leadership-based mergers read as residual transfers (43 cases). This is the main remaining gap. It is mostly chapters, union locals, auxiliaries, and plans sending their remaining assets to a parent or sister organization where officers already sat. Schedule N line 2 is answered yes, and Part VII shows overlap, but the overlap predates the transfer. - Part VII joiners (people new to the recipient after the merger) are more precise than overlap: 78% with a Schedule N flag, 55% without. Interlock-only cases without a flag score 45%. - Readers could not see Part VII, so this channel is not cleanly tested here.

Rule changes (v2, now the defaults). 1. min_top_share = 0.75, applied to the share of total FMV. It falls back to “one nonprofit recipient” only when FMV is missing. 2. final_as_termination = TRUE: a Part-II-only filing with the final-return box checked is treated as a termination. The new TERMINATED column records this. 3. sn_text = TRUE: SN_MERGER_TEXT (sn_merger_pattern() matched against asset descriptions, valuation methods, and Part III) counts as merger evidence on its own. BASIS = "sn_text".

v2 results (same sample).

classifier  hand merger transfer closure disposition reorg
merger 109 43 1 1 5
asset_transfer 6 26 5 0 2
closure 3 14 45 1 3
asset_disposition 4 1 2 29 0
  • Agreement: 70% (68% weighted).
  • Precision: merger 69% (62% weighted), asset transfer 67%, closure 68%, disposition 81%.
  • Merger recall rises from 51% to 71% (weighted).
  • Merger precision by basis: leader 70% (n = 149), sn_text 5/5, corroborated 0/5.
  • Population effect on 2010–2024: mergers go from 12,059 to 12,827 with promotion on, and to 12,346 with promotion off.
    • asset_disposition: 15,018 → 12,320.
    • asset_transfer: 10,180 → 9,548 (9,067 with promotion on).
    • closure: 22,978 → 26,021.
    • Promotion is now off by default (decided 2026-11-21), so 12,346 is the current count.

Other findings. - Closure → asset transfer (14). These are mostly single recipients with no EIN or name, such as “unnamed orphanage” or “another nonprofit”. They cannot become merger cases either way, so this mainly affects closure vs. transfer counts. - mergerN. Readers saw multi-party language in only 6% of mergerN cases. The label comes from other donors sending assets to the same recipient within a year. That is real, but it is usually a recipient absorbing several affiliates, not one multi-party deal; the text of a single filing rarely shows it. - consolidation. 54% of hand-read consolidations mention a new entity. - Reorganization. Readers found 10 (conversions, new EINs, PTA→PTO). The self-transfer rule catches none of them, because the new entity has a different EIN.

Still open. - Whether to keep promotion on by default: turned off (1 of 13 promoted filings read as mergers across v1 and v2). - Whether to define the Part VII channel as joiners rather than any overlap. - A human pass over the low-confidence labels.

6. Open questions

  1. 990-EZ donors. They are about half of Part I filers, but mostly tiny. Include them by default, with a size filter as an option?
  2. Year range. The current release (v3_1) covers 2009–2025, so the older v2_x releases are no longer needed. 2009 and 2025 are partial years.
  3. Fiscal index reference sample. Which reference should the fiscal-health model be calibrated on (section 7)?
